title: Probing the kinematics and chemistry of the hot core Mon R2 IRS 3 using ALMA observations
question: What is the physical, kinematical, and chemical structure of the massive protostellar hot core Mon R2 IRS 3 at high spatial resolution?

data.sensitivity: Continuum rms: 0.87 mJy/beam (1.2mm), 0.85 mJy/beam (1.1mm); Line rms: 0.102 to 0.211 K

what.value: N(13CO) = (1.1 +/- 0.2) x 10^17 cm^-2 from NIR absorption lines towards IRS 3 A

evidence.quote: (cite: Dungee2018) estimated N($^{13}$CO)=(1.1$\pm$0.2)$\times$10$^{17}$ cm$^{-2}$ based on the absorption NIR lines towards IRS 3 A.

what.value: Masses of the NIR protostars A, B, and C (25-37 M_sun)

evidence.quote: (cite: Preibisch2002) provided an estimation of the masses of the NIR protostars. Assuming that the NIR sources A, B and C are driving the toroid rotation, the stellar mass would be 25-37 M$_\odot$.

what.value: Molecular abundances for Orion and NGC 7129-IRS 2

evidence.quote: We have adopted the molecular abundances for Orion and NGC 7129$-$IRS 2 reported by (cite: Fuente2014).
Data for AFGL 2591 VLA 3 have been taken from (cite: Gieser2019).

recipe.goal: Construct continuum images, measure fluxes, fit 2D Gaussians, and derive dust/gas mass and H2 column density
recipe.method: Average line-free channels, merge visibilities of 247+257 GHz (1.2mm) and 262+272 GHz (1.1mm), fit two 2D Gaussians to the 1.1mm image, and apply a gray-body model to calculate mass and H2 column density.
assumptions: k_1.1mm = 0.0078 cm^2 g^-1, gas-to-dust ratio = 100, T_dust = 200 K

recipe.goal: Extract spectra and identify molecular lines
recipe.method: Extract interferometric spectra towards IRS 3 A and IRS 3 B and identify transitions above 4 sigma integrated intensity using CDMS and JPL spectroscopic catalogs.
key_parameters: Detection limit = 4 sigma in integrated intensity

recipe.goal: Analyze spatial distribution and gas kinematics using moment maps and PV diagrams
recipe.method: Compute zeroth-moment (integrated intensity) and first-moment (intensity-weighted velocity) maps, and extract Position-Velocity (PV) diagrams perpendicular to and along the reflection nebula axis to compare with Keplerian and solid-body rotation curves.
key_parameters: Reflection nebula direction P.A. ~ 40 deg; systemic velocity v_sys ~ 9 km s^-1
assumptions: Total stellar mass M_stars = 40 M_sun and inclination angle i = 45 deg for Keplerian comparison

recipe.goal: Derive rotation temperatures, molecular column densities, and fractional abundances
recipe.method: Apply the rotation diagram technique to SO2 and CH3OH lines to determine T_rot and column densities; fit LTE synthetic spectra at T_k = 129 K and 170 K for remaining species; compute abundances relative to N(H2).
key_parameters: T_k = 129 K and T_k = 170 K; upper limit linewidth = 4 km s^-1 and T_b < 3 x rms in 1 km s^-1 channel
assumptions: Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (LTE), N(H2) = 2.6 x 10^23 cm^-2, 12C/13C = 60, 16O/18O = 550, solar S/H = 1.5 x 10^-5

evidence.quote: Total fluxes are S(1.1mm)= 168$\pm$25 mJy and S(1.2mm)= 135$\pm$6 mJy, which implies a spectral index, $\alpha$=3.7$\pm$3.3, consistent with the emission being dominated by dust thermal emission.

answer_key.quantity: Total gas and dust mass of Mon R2 IRS 3

evidence.quote: Adopting T$_{\rm dust}$ = 200 K (see Sect. 4), we derive a total mass of $\sim$0.14 M$_\odot$.

answer_key.quantity: 1.1 mm Gaussian peak flux of IRS 3 A
1.1 mm Gaussian peak flux of IRS 3 B
Separation between IRS 3 A and IRS 3 B

evidence.quote: The continuum image at 1.1mm shows two components, IRS 3 A and IRS 3 B, that are separated by $\sim$0.65$"$.

answer_key.quantity: Averaged H2 column density towards IRS 3 A N(H2)

evidence.quote: We adopt the flux and the half power full size of the brightest Gaussian to estimate the averaged H$_2$ column density towards IRS 3 A, N(H$_2$)$\sim$2.6$\times$10$^{23}$ cm$^{-2}$.

answer_key.quantity: SO2 rotation temperature T_rot

evidence.quote: We obtained T$_{rot}$ = 175$_{-16}^{+15}$ K and N(SO$_2$)=3.4$_{-0.5}^{+0.6}$ $\times$ 10$^{16}$ cm$^{-2}$ using the three SO$_2$ lines observed towards IRS 3 A (see Table 2).

answer_key.quantity: SO2 column density N(SO2)

answer_key.quantity: CH3OH rotation temperature T_rot

evidence.quote: A slightly lower value of the rotation temperature, T$_{rot}$ = 129$_{-9}^{+10}$ K, and N(CH$_3$OH)=1.1$_{-0.2}^{+0.3}$ $\times$ 10$^{17}$ cm$^{-2}$, are found using the methanol lines.

answer_key.quantity: SO2 fractional abundance

answer_key.quantity: N(SO)/N(SO2) ratio

evidence.quote: The most abundant S-bearing species is SO$_2$ with an abundance of $\sim$ 1.3$\times$10$^{-7}$, and $\chi$(SO/SO$_2$) $\sim$ 0.29.
The N(SO)/N(SO$_2$) ratio is $\sim$0.29 in IRS 3 A similar to that observed in the Orion hot core and AFGL 2591 VLA 3

score_reason: Standard ALMA pipeline calibration (CASA 4.7) and clear spectral window/beam tables are provided, and LTE/rotational diagram analyses are straightforward, but specific imaging parameters, line-free channel definitions, spectral extraction apertures, and LTE source-size assumptions are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival ALMA data (2015.1.00453.S) with well-defined quantitative targets: 1.1 mm and 1.2 mm continuum fluxes, 2D Gaussian component parameters for IRS 3 A and B, rotational temperatures for SO2 and CH3OH, and LTE column densities for 16 molecular species.
